source: So, without further ado... a tale of espionage, subterfuge, and deception:
The Traitor of Spain!
It's not familiar to me, no.
This is wrong.
What do you mean, Hamlet?
This isn't what I—oh, never mind.
Our tale begins in the sunburnt city of Granada...
Where Queen Isabella and King Ferdinand wage war on the fearsome King Lucianus, even as Lucianus's country slides backwards into despair.
My lord Lucianus, the people are unhappy. What will you do?
I care not!
Oh, my lord, it will come to bite you in the end!
The King rules with God-given might, but there are thieves and liars in his court, and—even worse—a spy in his midst, leaking information to his enemies!
My lord, I love you with all my heart.
And I will make you my Queen, fair lady, if you answer me this: where do you go each night?
Oh! Merely to walk in the cold moonlight a while!
Even now, this traitorous woman claims to love her King, yet plots to slit his throat...
I love my King, but my country hates him so.
Surely another ruler could do better, wiser, stronger...
And on the night before Lucianus is to attack, she slips a dagger between his shoulders, thus sending all those who ever trusted her to ruin.
Think of how different the world might have been, had this girl not taken it upon herself to destroy a nation!
Hamlet, what are you doing?
What do you mean?
Quince, I think we've had enough of this play. It's troubling the tenderer ones amongst us, myself included.
As you wish, my lady.
I think the whole thing's terrible. Terrible and strange.
How topical.
It makes me shudder to think Brit of all people was going to betray us like that.
Art is a mirror to inspect life's deeper truths, is it not?
(It doesn't matter, though. I already know Brit's the one.)
So, without further ado, a thigh-slapping comedy of ineptitude...
The False Wise Man!
The... false wise man?
An, erm, a fascinating choice for a a performance. Yes, this ought to be interesting.
In the kingdom of a certain Lord Gonzago, there rests a terrible predicament...
He finds himself assaulted by his enemies at every step, embattled and in need of some good advice.
Woe be to him, though: He has only Corambis, the idiot advisor, at his side!
Corambis fails to 'inform' his master on even the simplest subjects.
I know not what I hunger for... Corambis, what ought I to eat for supper?
O, my lord, there is soup in the kitchen today! A most wonderful bone-broth of savory roots and meats.
But also, my lord, the cook has prepared a freshly-caught boar, and hanged it in the pantry for preparation tonight.
Of course, there's also a platter of sweetmeats on the hearth... and a roast duck in the guardhouse, and a hundred other things besides!
Corambis, I only wanted your best professional opinion. What good is a list of opportunities to me? I need a firm decision!
And if you can't help me with even this, old man, how are we ever supposed to win this god-awful war?
W-what? What is this?
Is that supposed to be... me?
One night, Corambis sneaks into the Queen's chambers to observe a most interesting conversation.
But as the exchange turns heated, he debates with himself: what ought he to do? Should he flee, or defend the Queen, or something more?
Unable to decide, he merely cries out—and gives away his position!
He's run through immediately. Poor Corambis. Dead too soon, and yet not dead soon enough!
O, I am slain!
That's a horrid caricature of me. Not like me at all.
Thus die I... thus... thus, thus!
Oh, for Heaven's sake.
Is this what the King and Queen think of me? Useless and rambling? Unable to perform my basic duties?
A-all these years, I thought I was good, and dutiful.
I've seen quite enough. Ladies, gentlemen, my lieges, please excuse me.
Goodness. Dearest, did you request that script?
Not at all. I hope Polonius didn't take offense.
Well, no mind. He'll recover. Good old Polonius, faithful as an aged drafthorse.
Quince, I think we've had quite enough. A wonderful performance. Thank you.
Of course, my lord. As you command!
(That wasn't the play I intended to perform.)
(Not in the slightest. I can't trust that Quince fellow at all.)
So, without further ado... a surreal tale, of destiny and circumstance!
The Goat's Song!
What on earth is this? And what on earth is a goat's song?
It's another way to call something a tragedy.
This isn't what Quince and I agreed upon at all...
In the kingdom of a certain Lord Gonzago, there rests a terrible predicament.
Every morning he wakes up, and like a good ruler, attends to his duties.
Yet every night, when he goes to sleep, he wakes up on the very same day once more.
The poor King reflects upon his situation...
I am trapped here, it seems, for worse or for ill.
Doomed to see the same dawn a thousand times or more!
What ails you, my lord, my love?
Fret not, my dear Baptista. I could not make you understand.
As the years pass—and yet pass not at all—madness overtakes him.
No matter what I try, when I open my eyes again, there my wife lies beside me, as peaceful as a lamb!
Unaware of the pain I've suffered, the madness I've endured, caught between life and death—
This is a strange performance. I'm not certain I follow.
S-something about an endless day, my love? It's confusing to me, as well.
Stop this, Quince. We're yawning ourselves into the grave down here.
From where did you find the inspiration for this terrible story?
Why, from the dear Ophelia herself. She came to me and asked me to spin this tale.
Hrm. From Ophelia?
How peculiar. It's unlike her to suggest something this... odd.
Your majesties, I merely meant to highlight something fantastical. Think nothing of it.
(I do worry about the girl's tendencies. She may become hysterical.)
(D-do you think we ought to call the physician?)
(Let's discuss this in private, dearest.)
So, without further ado, a surreal tale, of destiny and circumstance!
(Maybe this is the play he was 'meant' to perform before Hamlet got to him.)
(Or—perhaps it's something else entirely.)
But... where is everyone?
I know what you're doing.
Well, I should hope so. Couldn't be more blatant if I tried!
And what are you trying to achieve with this?
My dear girl, everything I do in this world is but a pathetic move to entertain myself a little before death eventually gets me.
Isn't that true of all human beings?
Isn't that true of you as well?
Entertainment? You call this entertainment?
Oh, maybe not for you. Certainly for me!
But I think the show's rather over, isn't it?
What a disappointing performance. I didn't even reach the beautiful conclusion!
I don't know how to do this.
Are you even listening, Lord?
Oh my offense is rank. It smells to Heaven.
Even if you cannot forgive me...
I can't bear this alone, not anymore.
I killed my brother.
The oldest crime, and the worst.
The castle believes it to be a snake bite which froze his blood as he slept in the garden.
B-but I poured that poison into his ear myself. I remember the feel of it in my hands.
I don't deserve anything of his. Not this crown, not my wife, none of it. I know it. I know I was wrong.
But in that moment, i-it felt... You know my heart, don't you, Lord? I could see no other way out.
I need salvation. Yet I am beyond salvation. All those who murder must go to hell. So your divine hand has written. Is it even possible to save my soul?
(How can it be? Is it really true?)
(So you murdered my father, eh? Now you die for it.)
God, please save me.
Save me from myself.
Surely you didn't forget me when you made me, Lord?
Surely there is still some hope for a sinner, a murderer like me?
(If I kill him while praying--)
(He's a lunatic. He confessed to murdering my father. I should kill him.)
(But if I do it now, while he's praying, he'll go to Heaven--)
(I can't. I can't do it.)
I should go.
I'm going to be ill. I can't stay here.
(It's exactly as my daughter warned me—he's—he's gone insane—)
(I need to leave—!)
He must be disciplined. This has gone on too long.
Now, my lady, the time has long since passed to talk sense into him.
He's made a fool of the King. You've been far too graceful.
Please, be honest with him—
Out. Out, Polonius. Now. I cannot bear to listen to you right now. Please.
(I'll not leave yet.)
Hamlet. You have been truly terrible to your uncle today.
And you have been truly terrible to my father.
What on earth?
This is her final chance to prove her loyalty and renounce her sin.
I think you know why I'm here, don't you? Why the play had to show that awful scene?
I don't understand.
Patience, Hamlet.
This ghost whispers patience in my ear. Father, how can you ask for patience?
You are seeing... spirits?
My father's ghost stands right there! Can you not see him? He comes to pass judgement! Do you not understand Claudius's sin?
Are you trying to say you don't know what he's done? After you married him?
I have no idea what you're talking about. My love, please, why are you shouting at me?
This is just another trap to try and convince me I'm insane.
No, Hamlet, it's not! Please, you must be mad—
You vile woman. You won't escape punishment.
Help! Someone, stop him!
What was that?
Are you and Claudius... spying on me?
Die, rat.
(I'm sorry...)
Hamlet, Hamlet, what have you done?
I took him for his better.
I warned you to stay your hand. It's happened again.
Ergh. Damn it.
You! You put him up to this!
Hamlet, I didn't know he was there, I swear!
Please, darling. Stop this.
Claudius murdered my father. He murdered my father, you suspected it, and yet you still slept with him!
I should let the whole castle know we have a whore for a Queen!
He did what?
Hamlet. Leave her. She is not your enemy. See how amazement sits upon her face. Speak to her gently.
No, Father. I need to do this!
Claudius... killed Hamlet?
Father is dead because of that snake.
I don't understand. How could he?
You're saying you... truly didn't know?
Can you not tell she is innocent?
Father, enough. Stop whispering in my ear!
Father's spirit implores me to show you mercy.
